title: Bill to align competition rules for Singapore's media and telecom sectors
what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading that amends the Info-communications Media Development Authority Act to harmonise competition rules for the telecommunications and media sectors and strengthen IMDA's regulatory toolkit.
why_it_matters: The Bill is intended to protect consumer interests by keeping the media market competitive and fair, with public confidence, good content, reasonable prices and a vibrant information environment. It also gives IMDA tools to act when fair market conduct is threatened and where service providers' actions may hurt consumer interests. The transcript also notes that workers may face disruption from mergers or restructurings, and that MOM frameworks and union engagement continue.

key_points.point: Mr Lee Hong Chuang rose to support the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
key_points.quote: I rise to support the Info-communications Media Development Authority (Amendment) Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Lee said the Bill brings greater consistency and clarity to competition regulation in both the media and telecommunications sectors.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
key_points.quote: this Bill brings greater consistency and clarity to the regulation of competition in both the media and telecommunications sectors.

key_points.point: Mr Lee said the Bill strengthens oversight over changes in control.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
key_points.quote: this Bill strengthens oversight over changes in control, and that is necessary.

key_points.point: Mr Lee said the Bill introduces the power for the Minister to issue separation orders in specific circumstances.
key_points.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang
key_points.quote: this Bill also introduces the power for the Minister to issue separation orders in specific circumstances.

key_points.point: Ms Cassandra Lee said the Bill seeks to further harmonise and align the competition frameworks governing the telecommunications and media sectors.
key_points.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee
key_points.quote: the IMDA (Amendment) Bill seeks to further harmonise and align the competition frameworks governing the telecommunications and media sectors.

key_points.point: Ms Cassandra Lee said the Bill's strengthening of competition oversight relates to ownership, control and market conduct.
key_points.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee
key_points.quote: the Bill's strengthening of competition oversight is particularly in relation to ownership, control and market conduct and this is both timely and necessary.

key_points.point: Ms Cassandra Lee said that under the proposed amendments, only provisions found to be anti-competitive will be void, while the rest of the agreement remains valid and enforceable.
key_points.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee
key_points.quote: Under the proposed amendments, only the provisions found to be anti-competitive will be void, with the remainder of the agreement continuing to be valid and enforceable.

key_points.point: Ms Cassandra Lee asked whether the competition framework may in time need to extend to entities that perform media-like functions outside traditional licensing categories.
key_points.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee
key_points.quote: could the Minister share whether the Ministry is considering whether aspects of this competition framework may in time need to extend to entities that perform media-like functions even if they do not fall within traditional licensing categories?

key_points.point: Ms Cassandra Lee asked for updates on whether further developments are being considered for the regulation of social media use by adolescents and youths.
key_points.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee
key_points.quote: I would like to ask if the Ministry would share any updates on whether it is considering any further developments in relation to the regulation of social media use by adolescents and youths.

key_points.point: Mr Tan Kiat How said the amendments strengthen the regulatory toolkit to ensure fair competition and market conduct in the media sector and protect consumer interests.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: They strengthen our regulatory toolkit to ensure fair competition and market conduct in the media sector and protect consumer interests.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the Bill is not about content regulation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: this Bill is not about content regulation.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the definitions of associate and effective control mirror existing definitions in the Telecommunications Act.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: They mirror existing definitions in the Telecommunications Act.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the definition of essential resources is in substance the same as the existing definition in the current IMDA Act.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: is in substance the same as the existing definition in the current IMDA Act.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the definition of regulated person continues to be targeted at key media entities and only covers entities specified by the Minister in the Gazette.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: The definition continues to be targeted at key media entities and only covers entities specified by the Minister in the Gazette.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the power to issue directions under the new section 61A is limited to maintaining fair market conduct, effective competition and safeguarding consumer interests.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: the power is limited to maintaining fair market conduct and effective competition and safeguarding consumer interests.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the new section 65A allows IMDA to require the disposal of shares or the relinquishment of control.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: this provision allows IMDA to require the disposal of shares or the relinquishment of control.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said structural separations are intended to be imposed only as a last resort and in exceptional cases.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: It is our intent that structural separations are only imposed as a last resort and in exceptional cases.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the first requirement for a separation order is a qualifying market condition.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: First, there must be a qualifying market condition.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the second requirement is that conventional regulatory remedies by IMDA have already been exhausted or are demonstrably inadequate.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Second, a separation order cannot be invoked by the Minister unless conventional regulatory remedies by IMDA have already been exhausted or are demonstrably inadequate.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the third requirement is that the Minister must be independently satisfied that issuing the separation order is in the public interest.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Third, the Minister must be independently satisfied that issuing the separation order is in the public interest.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the new section 69A(4) requires the Minister to ensure that the specific directions in a separation order are proportionate.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: The new section 69A(4) will require the Minister to ensure that the specific directions included in the separation order are proportionate.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said reconsideration and appeal mechanisms are already well established in the telecommunication sector since the market was fully liberalised in April 2000.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Both mechanisms are already well established in the telecommunication sector, since the market was fully liberalised in April 2000.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said MDDI and IMDA received one submission from a law firm directly relevant to the Bill during public consultation.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: MDDI and IMDA received one submission from a law firm directly relevant to the Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the amendments contribute to public confidence in the media sector, good content, reasonable prices and a vibrant information environment for every Singaporean.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: They contribute to public confidence in the media sector, good content, reasonable prices and a vibrant information environment for every Singaporean.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the amendments in the Bill do not pertain to social media regulation for adolescents and youths, and referred Ms Cassandra Lee to earlier replies and subsequent Parliamentary Questions.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: As the amendments of this Bill do not pertain to these specific matters, I would refer Ms Lee to those replies and to raise subsequent Parliamentary Questions if needed.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said unionised companies undergoing major organisational restructurings are encouraged to engage NTUC and their unions early.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: we encourage unionised companies embarking on or undergoing major organisational restructurings to engage the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and their unions early

key_points.point: Mr Tan said regulated persons include major players such as SPH Media Trust, Mediacorp and Pay TV operators, and that this approach is not being changed.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: These include major players, including SPH Media Trust, Mediacorp and our Pay TV operators. We are not making changes to this approach.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said IMDA's International Co-Production Fund supports local production houses.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: IMDA's International Co-Production Fund supports local production houses

key_points.point: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre asked whether the scope of regulated persons potentially includes social media companies and foreign players with a local presence.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: I also specifically had asked if this IMDA Bill, together with the Broadcasting Act that also is being amended, read together, does the scope of the regulated persons potentially include social media companies, foreign players, but that have a local presence?

key_points.point: Mr Low asked for clarification that the public interest wording in section 61A is not intended to be read independently as a broad power.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: I would appreciate if Senior Minister of State Tan can clarify that that is not the intent.

key_points.point: Mr Low asked whether the Government will commit not to direct that a separated business be transferred to a Government-linked media company.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: I had asked specifically if the Government will commit to not directing independent media companies that have been subject to a separation order, to then have that business transferred to a Government-linked media company.

key_points.point: Mr Low asked whether companies subject to a separation order will be obligated to reapply for their newspaper or broadcasting licence.
key_points.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
key_points.quote: If you read section 69A (3)b(ii) of the Bill, it seems to imply that companies that have been subject to a separation order will be obligated to reapply for their newspaper licence or broadcasting licence as the case may be.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said nothing in the amendment Bill touches the Broadcasting Act.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Nothing in this amendment Bill touches the Broadcasting Act.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said the regulatory intent is fair market competition and protecting consumer interest.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: The regulatory intent is for fair market competition and protecting consumer interest.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said nothing in the amendment Act changes the other Acts governing the media sector, including the Newspaper and Printing Presses Act or the Broadcasting Act.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: nothing in this amendment Act changes the other Acts that govern the media sector, whether the Newspaper and Printing Presses Act or the Broadcasting Act.

key_points.point: Mr Tan said that if entities need to apply for licences or permits to operate, they should do so.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: if they need to apply for licences, if they need apply for a permit to operate, they should do so.

key_points.point: Mr Pritam Singh raised a point of order about the Senior Minister of State referring to a speech by Ms Mariam Jaafar, who did not deliver a speech in Parliament on the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
key_points.quote: I believe the Senior Minister of State, in his wrapping-up speech, referred to a speech made by a Member who did not deliver a speech in Parliament on the Bill, that is, hon Member Ms Mariam Jaafar.

key_points.point: Mr Speaker said any Member who wishes to make a point must be in Parliament to make his or her speech.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: Any Member who wishes to make a point must be in Parliament to make his or her speech.

not_said: Will the Bill be passed, amended or referred to a committee, and on what timetable?
Where is the threshold between a small player and a regulated key media entity?
Do social media companies, foreign players with a local presence, blogs, social media accounts or podcasts fall within the scope of regulated persons?
How will the phrase in the public interest in section 61A be read alongside the preceding provisions?
Will the Government commit not to transfer a separated business to a Government-linked media company?
Will successor entities after a separation order have to reapply for newspaper or broadcasting licences, and on what criteria?
What further regulation of social media use by adolescents and youths is being considered?
What specific timelines and processes apply to reconsideration and appeal under the new sections 67A and 68?
How will workforce support be delivered beyond existing MOM frameworks and union engagement?
Will the competition framework be extended to non-traditional media entities that perform media-like functions?
What practical guidance or plain-language materials will IMDA provide for small and medium media enterprises?
What categories and examples will subsidiary legislation set out for transactions that must be notified to IMDA?
